references.text: Concerns the circumcision of purchased slaves and those born in the house, making them part of the household and covenant community.
Abraham circumcised all the men in his household, including those bought with money and those born in the house.
The previous verse establishes the context regarding who may not eat of the holy things, in contrast to verse 11 which addresses who may.
Legislation concerning the purchase of slaves from foreign nations, who become property and inheritance for the Israelites.
A purchased slave who is circumcised may eat of the Passover lamb, showing that bought slaves could participate in holy meals.
Describes who in the priest's household may eat of the holy offerings, including daughters living at home.
